source_text:
ἀποφήνασθαι τὸν Κύριον, ὡς «οἱ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τευξόμενοι ἔσονται τότε ὡς ἄγγελοι,» ἔνθα πειράζουσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι, ἐπέφερεν· «Οἱ δὲ ἄγγελοι ἐκτὸς
ὄντες σαρκὸς ἐν μακαριότητος ἀκρότητι, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ δόξης εἰσί· καὶ ἡμᾶς δὲ ἄρα
ἐξισάζεσθαι μέλλοντας ἀγγέλοις ἀνάγκη δὴ σαρκῶν ὡσαύτως ἐκείνοις γυμνοὺς
ἔσεσθαι δεῖν.»
pass_a_gloss: to declare the Lord, as "those who will attain the resurrection will then be as angels," where the Sadducees tempt him, he added: "But the angels, being outside flesh in the height of blessedness, for this reason are also of glory; and we therefore, being about to be equalized to angels, must likewise need to be bare of flesh as they are."
pass_b_english: …to declare the Lord, as when the Sadducees tempt him: "[[those who attain the resurrection will then be as angels >> Bible:Luke 20:36]]." He adds: "Angels stand outside flesh in the height of blessedness, and for that reason they also have glory; so we who are to be made equal to angels must likewise be bare of flesh as they are."

choices.choice: PG 11 De Resurrectione (Khazarzar); locked rem close Greek.
Methodius reports Origen extending Luke 20:36 toward fleshless glory.
Temptation setting kept; quotation framed as Origen's addition.
